easy.def: To copy by following lines.
examples: Trace the picture.
She traced her hand.
He traces the letters.

more.def: To copy a drawing by following its lines on thin paper.
examples: Trace the picture with a pencil.
She traced her hand on the paper.
He traced the map onto a clear sheet.

easy.def: A small sign that something was there.
examples: There was no trace of the cat.
A trace of snow.
A trace of dust.

more.def: A small mark or sign that something was there.
examples: There was no trace of the missing cat.
A trace of snow stayed on the roof.
The detective found a trace of mud.

easy.def: Marks left by an animal's feet.
examples: We saw deer tracks.
There were tracks in the snow.
The dog left muddy tracks.

more.def: Marks or prints left on the ground by a person, animal or vehicle.
examples: We followed the deer tracks through the snow.
The dog left muddy tracks across the floor.
Tire tracks led to the barn.

easy.def: Rails for trains.
examples: The train is on the track.
The tracks go by the river.
Do not play on the tracks.

more.def: The metal rails that a train runs on.
examples: The train tracks run along the river.
A freight train rumbled over the tracks.
The tracks curved around the hill.

easy.def: A path for racing.
examples: The runners ran on a track.
The school has a track.
There is a track around the field.

more.def: A path, often shaped like an oval, where people or cars race.
examples: She ran four laps around the track.
The race cars sped around the track.
The school track is next to the soccer field.

easy.def: To follow marks to find something.
examples: Wolves track their food.
We tracked the deer.
The dog tracked the scent.

more.def: To follow marks, signs or a scent to find someone or something.
examples: The ranger tracked the bear by its paw prints.
A dog can track a scent for miles.
Scientists track whales with tiny radios.

easy.def: To swap one thing for another.
examples: Let's trade cards.
I traded my pencil.
She trades stickers.

more.def: To give something and get something else in return.
examples: Let's trade lunches today.
I traded my stickers for his marbles.
She trades baseball cards with her friend.

easy.def: Buying and selling.
examples: Trade between countries.
The trade of goods.
Trade is busy.

more.def: The buying and selling of goods.
examples: The port is busy with trade.
Trade between the two countries grew.
Ships carried goods for trade.

easy.def: Something a family or group does again and again over many years.
examples: It is our tradition to bake a cake on birthdays.
Our tradition is to eat pancakes on Sunday.
It is a tradition to sing that song.

more.def: A belief or way of doing things that is passed down in a family or group over time.
examples: It is a tradition in her family to tell stories around the fire every winter.
The school has a tradition of planting a tree every year.
By tradition, the oldest child lights the candles.

easy.def: Cars and trucks moving on a road.
examples: There is a lot of traffic today.
We waited for the traffic to stop.
The traffic is slow near the school.

more.def: The cars, buses and trucks moving along a road or street at one time.
examples: Heavy traffic made us late for the game.
A police officer directed traffic after the storm.
Traffic moves slowly on rainy days.

easy.def: A path through the woods or hills.
examples: We hiked a trail.
The trail was muddy.
The trail goes up the mountain.

more.def: A rough path through the countryside, made by people or animals.
examples: We followed the trail through the woods.
Hikers walked along a rocky trail up the mountain.
A trail of footprints led to the door.

easy.def: A line of cars that runs on tracks.
examples: We rode a train.
The train is long.
A train goes through the town.

more.def: A line of connected cars pulled along a track, carrying people or goods.
examples: The train rolled slowly out of the station.
A freight train carries coal and grain across the country.
We took the train to see the city.

easy.def: To teach someone a skill by practicing.
examples: I train my dog.
She trains for the race.
He is training to swim.

more.def: To teach a person or animal a skill, or to practice to get better.
examples: She trained her puppy to sit and stay.
The runners train every morning for the big race.
Doctors train for many years before they work.

easy.def: Learning how to do something by practicing.
examples: He is in training for the race.
Dog training.
She got training for the job.

more.def: The process of learning a skill by practicing it.
examples: He is in training for the big race.
The puppy is in training class.
Nurses need years of training.

easy.def: To move from one place to another.
examples: Transfer the water to a jug.
He transferred schools.
She transferred the money.

more.def: To move something or someone from one place to another.
examples: Transfer the soup into a bowl.
She transferred to a new school.
Dad transferred the photos to the computer.

easy.def: Clear, so you can see through it.
examples: Glass is transparent.
The fish tank is transparent.
A transparent bag lets you see inside.

more.def: Clear enough that you can see through it.
examples: The jellyfish was almost transparent in the water.
Tape the transparent plastic over the window.
The water was so transparent that we could see the bottom.

easy.def: Something set up to catch an animal.
examples: The trap caught a mouse.
He set a trap.
The fox escaped the trap.

more.def: A device or hole used to catch animals.
examples: Dad set a trap for the mouse in the shed.
The fox escaped from the trap.
The hunters dug a trap in the story.

easy.def: To catch or hold something so it cannot get out.
examples: The net trapped the fish.
I was trapped in the elevator.
The bear was trapped.

more.def: To catch or hold something so that it cannot escape.
examples: The fishing net trapped the fish.
A fallen tree trapped the car.
We were trapped inside by the snow.

easy.def: Things you throw away.
examples: Put the paper in the trash.
The trash can is full.
I took out the trash.

more.def: Things that are thrown away because no one wants them, like old paper or empty cans.
examples: The park was clean, with no trash on the ground.
Please put your wrappers in the trash.
We sorted the trash into paper, plastic and cans.

easy.def: To go from one place to another.
examples: We travel to the beach by car.
We travel by bus.
Birds travel far in the fall.

more.def: To go from one place to another, often over a long distance.
examples: They traveled across the country by train.
Light travels faster than sound.
My aunt travels to many countries for her job.

easy.def: Gold, gems, or other special things.
examples: The pirates hid the treasure.
The map shows where the treasure is.
My rock is a treasure to me.

more.def: Valuable things such as gold and jewels, or something very special to you.
examples: The divers found treasure in the sunken ship.
The museum's greatest treasure is a golden mask.
Grandma's letters are a treasure to our family.

easy.def: Something special to eat.
examples: Ice cream is a treat.
We got a treat.
The dog got a treat.

more.def: Something special that gives you pleasure, such as a snack or a trip.
examples: Ice cream is a treat on a hot day.
Going to the zoo was a special treat.
The dog gets a treat when it sits.

easy.def: To act toward someone in a certain way.
examples: She treats her dog like a friend.
Treat the new toy with care.
Dad treats us fairly.

more.def: To behave toward a person or animal in a certain way.
examples: The nurse treated the little boy kindly.
Treat the old books with care.
They treat their pets like family.

easy.def: To give care to a sick person.
examples: The doctor treats sick people.
The vet treated my dog's paw.
Nurses treat patients.

more.def: To give medicine or care to help a sick or hurt person or animal.
examples: The nurse treated the cut on my knee.
Doctors treat many kinds of illness.
The vet treated the horse's sore leg.

easy.def: Care that helps a sick person get better.
examples: The doctor gave her a treatment.
Rest is the best treatment.
The treatment worked.

more.def: The care or medicine a doctor gives to help someone get well.
examples: The doctor gave her a treatment for her cough.
Rest and warm soup were the best treatment for his cold.
The vet gave the dog treatment for its sore paw.

easy.def: A tall plant with a trunk and branches.
examples: A bird sits in the tree.
The tree has green leaves.
We climbed the tree.

more.def: A tall plant with a thick wooden trunk, branches and leaves.
examples: A squirrel ran up the tree.
The oak tree is over a hundred years old.
We planted a tree in the backyard.

easy.def: To shake a little.
examples: My hands tremble when I am cold.
The puppy trembled in the cold.
My voice trembles when I am scared.

more.def: To shake slightly because you are cold, afraid, or excited.
examples: The leaves trembled in the gentle wind.
The ground trembled as the train passed.
His hands trembled as he opened the letter.

easy.def: A time in court when a judge decides a case.
examples: The trial lasted a week.
The judge led the trial.
People watched the trial.

more.def: A meeting in a court where a judge or jury decides if someone broke the law.
examples: The trial lasted three days.
The lawyer spoke at the trial.
The jury listened carefully during the trial.

easy.def: A test to see how well something works.
examples: The trial of the new bike went well.
We did a trial run.
The medicine was in a trial.

more.def: A test of something to find out how well it works.
examples: Scientists ran a trial of the new medicine.
We did a trial run before the big show.
The toy had a one-week trial.

easy.def: Something done to fool someone.
examples: The magician did a trick.
Hiding the cookie was a trick.
It was a trick!

more.def: Something done to fool or surprise people.
examples: The magician showed us a card trick.
Hiding the cookie was a clever trick.
It was a trick to make me look away.

easy.def: A special thing that a pet or person can do.
examples: My dog can do a trick.
She learned a card trick.
He did a trick on his bike.

more.def: A skillful act done to entertain or amaze.
examples: The dog's best trick is rolling over.
He practiced a trick on his skateboard.
The clown's tricks made everyone laugh.

easy.def: To fool someone.
examples: You cannot trick me.
He tricked his friend.
The fox tricked the crow.

more.def: To fool someone by being clever.
examples: The fox tricked the crow into dropping its cheese.
The magician tricked the audience.
My brother tried to trick me with a fake spider.

easy.def: To make something start.
examples: A loud noise can trigger the alarm.
The smoke triggered the alarm.
The storm triggered a power failure.

more.def: To cause something to start or happen.
examples: A tiny bug on the sensor triggered the alarm.
Heavy rain triggered a flood in the valley.
The funny joke triggered a burst of laughter.

easy.def: A part you press to make something work.
examples: He pressed the trigger on the camera.
The trigger is on the nozzle.
I pulled the trigger of the spray bottle.

more.def: A small lever or button that you press to start a machine working.
examples: She pulled the trigger on the spray bottle.
The camera's trigger takes the picture.
The trigger on the water gun is easy to press.

easy.def: When you go somewhere and come back.
examples: We took a trip to the zoo.
Our trip to the lake was fun.
The trip took two hours.

more.def: A journey to a place and back.
examples: Our class took a trip to the science museum.
The trip to Grandma's house takes three hours.
We packed lunches for the trip.

easy.def: To catch your foot and almost fall.
examples: Do not trip on the rug.
I tripped over a root.
He tripped on the step.

more.def: To catch your foot on something and almost fall.
examples: She tripped over a toy in the hall.
Be careful not to trip on the root.
The runner tripped but quickly got back up.

easy.def: A hard time, or something that goes wrong.
examples: I am in trouble.
We had trouble.
No trouble at all.

more.def: A difficult time or something that causes problems.
examples: The boat had engine trouble, so we stopped at the dock.
I had trouble tying my shoes when I was little.
He got into trouble for running in the hall.

easy.def: A big vehicle that carries things.
examples: The truck carries sand.
The fire truck came.
The truck delivers food.

more.def: A large motor vehicle used to carry goods.
examples: A truck delivered the new couch.
The garbage truck comes every Thursday.
Dad drives a truck full of apples.

easy.def: Real, and not pretend.
examples: It is a true story.
Is that true?
She told the true thing.

more.def: Real and correct, and not made up or false.
examples: It is true that the Earth goes around the sun.
The book tells a true story about a brave dog.
Is it true that bats can see in the dark?

easy.def: The thick main part of a tree.
examples: The tree trunk is wide.
A squirrel ran up the trunk.
We hugged the tree trunk.

more.def: The thick main stem of a tree, from which the branches grow.
examples: A squirrel scurried up the tree trunk.
The trunk of the old oak was too wide to hug.
Moss grew on one side of the trunk.

easy.def: An elephant's long nose.
examples: The elephant used its trunk to drink.
An elephant sprayed water with its trunk.
The baby held its mother's tail with its trunk.

more.def: The long, flexible nose of an elephant, used for smelling, drinking and picking things up.
examples: The elephant sprayed water with its trunk.
She fed a peanut to the elephant, which took it with its trunk.
An elephant uses its trunk like a hand.

easy.def: A big box with a lid used for storing things.
examples: The old toys are in the trunk.
Grandma keeps blankets in a trunk.
A trunk was at the foot of the bed.

more.def: A large box with a lid used for storing or carrying things, or the storage space at the back of a car.
examples: He put the bags in the trunk of the car.
Grandpa's old trunk is full of photographs.
The pirates hid the treasure in a wooden trunk.

easy.def: To feel sure that someone is good and honest.
examples: I trust my mom.
I trust my friend to keep a secret.
The dog trusts me.

more.def: To believe that someone is honest and will not hurt you or let you down.
examples: You can trust her to keep a promise.
Do you trust the weather report?
It takes time to trust someone new.

easy.def: What is real and not pretend.
examples: Tell the truth, please.
The truth is that I forgot my lunch.
He told the truth about the broken cup.

more.def: The facts about something as they really are, not made up or false.
examples: The scientist looked for the truth by doing careful tests.
She told the truth about how the vase got broken.
There is a lot of truth in that old story.

easy.def: To work to do something.
examples: I try to jump high.
She tried again.
Try to be quiet.

more.def: To make an effort to do something, or to test something to see if you like it.
examples: I will try to finish my book before the weekend.
He tried a new kind of fruit at the market.
The baby is trying to take her first steps.
